scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands beside a plain table lamp on a table with one finger on the switch at the lamp base, and the lamp shines: five bold straight rays leave the shade and the shade has a bright inner outline. The adult looks at the lamp.
must: bold rays leaving the shade beside a finger on the switch.
avoid: the same lamp with no rays (uitdoen); an adult lighting a candle with a match (aansteken); a window with sun rays and no lamp (not the action); a ceiling bulb with nobody near it (not the action).
contrast: Pair with uitdoen. The only difference is the lamp: rays round the shade here, no rays there.
example_nl: Ik doe de lamp aan.
alt: Een volwassene houdt een vinger op de schakelaar van een tafellamp en uit de kap komen stralen.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands beside the same plain table lamp with one finger on the switch at the lamp base, and the lamp is dark: no rays, a plain shade with an empty outline. The adult looks at the lamp. The room and table are unchanged.
must: a plain unlit shade with no rays beside a finger on the switch.
avoid: the same lamp with rays (aandoen); a lamp knocked over on the table (omvallen); an adult blowing out a candle (uitblazen); a lamp with a cloth thrown over it (not the action).
contrast: Pair with aandoen. The only difference is the lamp: no rays at all here, bold rays there.
example_nl: Ik doe de lamp uit.
alt: Een volwassene houdt een vinger op de schakelaar van een tafellamp en de kap is leeg en vlak.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands beside a small radio on a shelf with one hand turning the round knob, and from the radio come three bold curved sound lines and two small music notes. The adult smiles slightly and looks at the radio.
must: curved sound lines and notes from the radio beside a hand on the knob.
avoid: the same radio with no lines (uitzetten); an adult with a hand cupped to an ear (not the card); an adult singing with a speech bubble (not the card); a radio lying on its side (not the action).
contrast: Pair with uitzetten. The only difference is the radio: sound lines and notes here, none there.
example_nl: Ik zet de radio aan.
alt: Een volwassene draait aan een knop van een radio en er komen golvende lijnen en noten uit.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands beside the same small radio on a shelf with one hand on the round knob, and the radio is silent: no sound lines, no notes, the speaker plain. The adult looks at the radio with a neutral face.
must: a plain radio with no sound lines beside a hand on the knob.
avoid: the same radio with sound lines and notes (aanzetten); an adult unplugging a cable from the wall (loskoppelen); an adult with fingers in both ears (not the action); a radio on a high shelf out of reach (not the action).
contrast: Pair with aanzetten. The only difference is the radio: no lines or notes here, three lines and two notes there.
example_nl: Ik zet de radio uit.
alt: Een volwassene houdt een hand op de knop van een radio en de radio is stil.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands beside the door frame holding the round handle with the door swung wide open towards the viewer, so the dark doorway and the thickness of the door are visible. No key is in the keyhole. The adult looks into the doorway.
must: a door swung wide with a dark gap beside the adult's hand on the handle.
avoid: the same door flat shut (dichtdoen); the same door shut with a key turned in the lock (afsluiten); a door open only a crack (not the card); a window opened wide (not the card).
contrast: Pair with dichtdoen and afsluiten. The only difference is the door: swung wide here, flat in its frame there.
example_nl: Ik doe de deur open.
alt: Een volwassene staat naast een deur die wijd naar binnen staat en kijkt in het donkere deurgat.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands beside the door frame with one hand flat on the door and the door sitting flat in its frame with no gap showing; the round handle is level and the keyhole is empty. A short motion line shows the door has just swung.
must: the door flat in its frame with no gap and a motion line.
avoid: the same door swung wide (opendoen); the same door with a key turned in the keyhole (afsluiten); an adult slamming the door with a cartoon burst (not the card); a closed window (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opendoen and afsluiten. The only difference is the door: flat shut with no key here, wide open there.
example_nl: Ik doe de deur dicht.
alt: Een volwassene legt een hand op een deur die vlak in de sponning zit en er is geen kier.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands beside the shut door and turns a plain key in the lock with one hand, the key clearly sticking out of the keyhole, the fingers round the key, and the door sitting flat in its frame. A small turning arrow curves round the key.
must: a key turning in the keyhole of a shut door.
avoid: the same door shut with no key (dichtdoen); the same door open with a key in the lock (opendoen); an adult holding keys in a pocket (not the action); a padlock on a gate (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opendoen and dichtdoen. The only difference is the key: turning in the keyhole here, no key anywhere there.
example_nl: Ik sluit de deur af.
alt: Een volwassene draait een sleutel in een deur die vlak in de sponning zit.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands at a bed laying a folded shirt into an open suitcase; half the clothes are already inside the case and two more folded piles still lie on the bed. The adult's hands and the shirt are above the case, a small arrow pointing down into it.
must: a folded shirt going down into a half-full open suitcase.
avoid: the same suitcase being emptied onto the bed (uitpakken); an adult carrying a closed suitcase to a door (meenemen); a suitcase with a folded umbrella next to it (not the card); an adult folding a shirt on the bed with no suitcase (not the card).
contrast: Pair with uitpakken. The only difference is the direction: clothes going into the case here, coming out of it there.
example_nl: Ik pak mijn koffer in.
alt: Een volwassene legt een gevouwen overhemd in een open koffer op een bed.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands at a bed lifting a folded shirt out of the same open suitcase; most clothes already lie in small piles on the bed and the case is nearly empty. The adult's hands and the shirt are above the bed, a small arrow pointing up out of the case.
must: a shirt lifted out of a nearly empty open suitcase.
avoid: the same suitcase being filled (inpakken); an adult opening a wrapped present (not the card); an adult hanging clothes on a rail (not the card); a shut suitcase on the floor (not the action).
contrast: Pair with inpakken. The only difference is the direction: clothes coming out of the case here, going into it there.
example_nl: Ik pak mijn koffer uit.
alt: Een volwassene haalt een gevouwen overhemd uit een bijna lege koffer en legt het op het bed.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A plain bus stands side-on at a stop with its middle doors open, and one adult has one foot on the bus step and the other still on the kerb, chest to the open doors and body leaning in, a small arrow pointing into the bus.
must: one foot on the bus step, chest to the open doors.
avoid: an adult stepping off the bus onto the kerb (uitstappen); an adult waiting on the bench (not the action); an adult driving the bus (not the card); an adult running behind a bus (not the card).
contrast: Pair with uitstappen. The only difference is the direction: stepping up into the bus here, down onto the kerb there.
example_nl: Ik stap bij de halte in.
example_en: I get on at the stop.
alt: Een volwassene zet een voet op de trede van een bus met open deuren en leunt naar binnen.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The same plain bus stands side-on at the stop with its middle doors open, and one adult has one foot on the kerb and the other still on the bus step, back to the open doors and body leaning out, a small arrow pointing out of the bus.
must: one foot on the kerb, back to the open doors.
avoid: an adult stepping up into the bus (instappen); an adult waving at a bus driving off (not the card); an adult sitting inside the bus (not the action); an adult climbing out of a car (not the card).
contrast: Pair with instappen. The only difference is the direction: stepping down onto the kerb here, up into the bus there.
example_nl: Ik stap bij het station uit.
example_en: I get off at the station.
alt: Een volwassene zet een voet op de stoeprand en heeft de rug naar de open deuren van een bus.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult sits at a table holding the handset of a desk phone against one ear, the other hand on the buttons, mouth slightly open as if speaking, and a thin curl of cable running from the handset to the phone on the table.
must: a handset held against the ear with the cable running to the phone.
avoid: the handset sitting on the cradle with nobody holding it (ophangen); an adult typing on a laptop (not the card); an adult speaking through a megaphone (not the card); an adult texting with both thumbs on a small phone (not the action).
contrast: Pair with ophangen. The only difference is the handset: at the ear here, down on its cradle there.
example_nl: Ik bel mijn vader op.
alt: Een volwassene aan een tafel houdt een hoorn tegen het oor en drukt met de andere hand op de toetsen.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult sits at the same table and lowers the handset of the desk phone onto its cradle with one hand, the handset a few centimetres above the cradle, the cable hanging in a loop, the adult's mouth closed.
must: a handset a hand's width above its cradle with the cable looped.
avoid: the handset held against the ear (opbellen); a coat hung on a wall hook (not this sense); a picture frame hung on a nail (not this sense); an adult putting the phone in a pocket (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opbellen. The only difference is the handset: lowered towards the cradle here, held to the ear there.
example_nl: Na het gesprek hang ik op.
example_en: After the call I hang up.
alt: Een volwassene laat de hoorn van een telefoon op de houder zakken en de mond blijft dicht.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A plain train carriage enters from the right edge of the picture, its nose and front door already beside the platform and the rest still off the page, a small arrow pointing left; on the platform an adult with a small suitcase faces the train's nose.
must: a train nose entering at the right edge with the adult facing it.
avoid: the train's tail leaving at the left edge (wegrijden); an adult walking along the platform (not the card); a bus at a stop (not the card); an adult stepping off the train (uitstappen).
contrast: Pair with wegrijden. The only difference is the train: its nose entering at the right edge here, its tail leaving at the left edge there.
example_nl: De trein komt om tien uur aan.
example_en: The train arrives at ten o'clock.
alt: Een trein stopt bij het perron en een volwassene met een koffer staat met het gezicht naar de voorkant van de trein.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The same plain train carriage leaves at the left edge of the picture, only its tail end still beside the platform and the front already off the page, a small arrow pointing left; the adult with a small suitcase stands behind it on the platform, hands down.
must: a train tail leaving at the left edge with the adult behind it.
avoid: the train's nose entering at the right edge (aankomen); an adult stepping off the train (uitstappen); a car pulling out of a drive (not the card); a bus at a stop with its doors open (instappen).
contrast: Pair with aankomen. The only difference is the train: its tail leaving at the left edge here, its nose entering at the right edge there.
example_nl: De trein rijdt om elf uur weg.
example_en: The train drives off at eleven o'clock.
alt: Een trein verlaat het station en alleen de achterkant staat nog naast het perron, met een volwassene erachter.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult steps out of the open front door towards the viewer and holds a closed umbrella in one hand by the curved handle, the other hand on the door; a small arrow points out of the doorway towards the viewer. The umbrella stand beside the door is empty.
must: an umbrella in the adult's hand at the door beside an empty stand.
avoid: the umbrella left standing in the stand as the adult leaves (achterlaten); an adult carrying a heavy box (optillen); an adult opening an umbrella in rain (not the card); an adult holding hands with a child (not the card).
contrast: Pair with achterlaten. The only difference is where the umbrella is: in the adult's hand here, standing in the stand there.
example_nl: Ik neem mijn paraplu mee.
example_en: I take my umbrella with me.
alt: Een volwassene staat bij de open voordeur met een paraplu in de hand en de paraplubak naast de deur is leeg.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult steps out of the open front door towards the viewer, hands empty and swinging, while a plain umbrella stays standing in the umbrella stand beside the door behind them. A small arrow points out of the doorway towards the viewer.
must: an umbrella standing in the stand as the empty-handed adult walks out.
avoid: the adult holding the umbrella in the doorway (meenemen); an umbrella dropped on a street (not the card); an adult hiding an umbrella in a cupboard (not the card); a locked door with nobody near it (afsluiten).
contrast: Pair with meenemen. The only difference is the umbrella: in the stand with an empty-handed adult here, in the adult's hand there.
example_nl: Ik laat mijn paraplu thuis achter.
example_en: I leave my umbrella at home.
alt: Een volwassene loopt met lege handen de voordeur uit terwijl een paraplu in de bak blijft staan.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult bends over the open toy box and lets a toy drop from one hand into it, a short downward arrow under the toy. The box is half full and two toys still lie on the floor beside the adult's feet.
must: a toy dropping into a half-full box with two toys still on the floor.
avoid: the same room with the floor being wiped with a cloth (schoonmaken); an adult throwing toys in a bin (weggooien); an adult counting toys on a shelf (not the card); an adult sweeping crumbs from a table (not the card).
contrast: Pair with schoonmaken. The only difference is the hands: a toy dropping into the box here, a cloth wiping the floor there.
example_nl: Ik ruim mijn kamer op.
alt: Een volwassene laat een speelgoedje in een halfvolle kist vallen en er liggen nog twee speelgoedjes op de vloer.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult kneels beside a bucket and wipes the floor with a cloth moving to one side. Ahead of the cloth lie small dirt flecks; behind it the floor is bare with three sparkle lines. The toy box stands shut in the background.
must: a cloth with dirt flecks ahead of it and sparkle lines behind it.
avoid: the same room with toys going into the box (opruimen); an adult washing dishes (afwassen); an adult sweeping with a broom and no cloth (not the card); an adult spraying a window (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opruimen. The only difference is the hands: a cloth wiping the floor here, a toy dropping into the box there.
example_nl: Ik maak de vloer schoon.
alt: Een volwassene boent met een doek over de vloer: voor de doek liggen vlekjes, achter de doek glanst de vloer.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands facing the viewer with one arm through a coat sleeve while the coat rises onto the second shoulder and the second arm slides into its sleeve, a small arrow pointing up beside the coat, the empty wall hook beside them.
must: a coat rising onto the second shoulder with an upward arrow.
avoid: the coat being pulled off over the shoulders (uittrekken); an adult holding a coat on a hanger (not the card); an adult tying a scarf (not the card); an adult pulling a rope (not the card).
contrast: Pair with uittrekken. The only difference is the coat: rising onto the shoulders with an arrow up here, down at the elbows with an arrow down there.
example_nl: Ik trek mijn jas aan.
alt: Een volwassene steekt de armen in de mouwen en de jas schuift omhoog over de schouders.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands facing the viewer with the coat pulled down off both shoulders to the elbows, both arms still in the sleeves, a small arrow pointing down beside the coat, the empty wall hook beside them.
must: a coat down at the elbows with a downward arrow.
avoid: the coat going on with one sleeve empty (aantrekken); an adult hanging a coat on the hook (not the card); a coat lying on the floor (not the card); an adult pulling a tooth (not the card).
contrast: Pair with aantrekken. The only difference is the coat: down at the elbows with an arrow down here, rising onto the shoulders with an arrow up there.
example_nl: Ik trek mijn jas uit.
alt: Een volwassene laat een jas van beide schouders tot de ellebogen zakken.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult rises off the edge of the bed, weight on both feet, knees straightening and hips lifted clear of the mattress, the blanket pushed back; the blank-faced alarm clock has two short ring lines and a low sun sits at the bottom of the window.
must: an adult rising off the mattress onto both feet with the alarm ringing.
avoid: an adult lying asleep in the bed with a blanket up to the chin (uitslapen); an adult sitting in a chair at a table (not the card); an adult standing up from a chair (not the card); an adult jumping on the bed (not the card).
contrast: Pair with uitslapen. The only difference is the sleeper: rising onto the feet with a ringing clock and low sun here, lying still with a silent clock and high sun there.
example_nl: Ik sta om zeven uur op.
example_en: I get up at seven o'clock.
alt: Een volwassene komt van het bed overeind op beide voeten en naast het bed rinkelt een wekker.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The same adult lies in the bed on one side with eyes closed and a content small smile, the blanket up to the chin; the blank-faced alarm clock is silent with no ring lines, and the sun stands high in the window with long rays.
must: a sleeper in bed under a high sun with a silent clock.
avoid: an adult sitting on the bed edge with a ringing clock (opstaan); an adult napping in an armchair (not the card); an adult lying awake with open eyes (not the card); a child jumping on the bed (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opstaan. The only difference is the sleeper: lying still under a high sun with a silent clock here, rising onto the feet with a ringing clock there.
example_nl: Op zondag slaap ik uit.
alt: Een volwassene ligt met gesloten ogen onder een deken, de zon is hoog en de wekker is stil.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands at the open back of a plain van lifting a box up onto the van floor, two boxes already stacked inside and one box still on the road beside the adult's feet, a small arrow pointing into the van.
must: a box being lifted up into the van with others already stacked inside.
avoid: boxes being carried out of the van onto the road (uitladen); an adult driving the van (not the card); an adult packing a suitcase (inpakken); an adult lifting one heavy box on an empty road (optillen).
contrast: Pair with uitladen. The only difference is the direction: boxes going up into the van here, down onto the road there.
example_nl: Ik laad de dozen in.
alt: Een volwassene schuift een doos in de achterkant van een bestelbus waar al twee dozen staan.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands at the open back of the same van lifting a box down from the van floor onto the road, two boxes already stacked on the road and one box still inside, a small arrow pointing out of the van.
must: a box being lowered from the van onto the road beside a stack on the ground.
avoid: boxes being lifted into the van (inladen); an adult unpacking clothes from a suitcase (uitpakken); a van parked with the doors shut (not the action); an adult pushing a trolley (not the card).
contrast: Pair with inladen. The only difference is the direction: boxes going down onto the road here, up into the van there.
example_nl: Ik laad de dozen bij de winkel uit.
example_en: I unload the boxes at the shop.
alt: Een volwassene haalt een doos uit de achterkant van een bestelbus en op de weg staan al twee dozen.

scene: SKIP: no separable opposite. landen is not separable and already has its card in Werkwoorden (a1-regular, landen), and neerkomen reads as a crash, so a one-verb set cannot show the contrast.
example_nl: Het vliegtuig stijgt op.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A small child stands inside the open school gate with a schoolbag on its back and one hand stretched up, and an adult stands outside on the pavement holding out a hand to take it. The child's schoolbag is on, the gate is open.
must: a child's raised hand meeting the adult's hand at the open gate.
avoid: the adult walking away while the child goes in through the gate (wegbrengen); an adult carrying a box (optillen); an adult waving goodbye to a bus (not the card); a child running alone (not the card).
contrast: Pair with wegbrengen. The only difference is the direction: the adult reaches in to collect the child here, and leaves the child inside there.
example_nl: Ik haal mijn zoon van school op.
example_en: I pick up my son from school.
alt: Een kind met een schooltas staat bij een open hek en een volwassene aan de andere kant pakt zijn hand.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A small child with a schoolbag walks in through the open school gate looking back, and an adult stands on the pavement outside with a raised waving hand and one foot turned away from the gate. The adult's hands are empty.
must: an adult's waving hand outside the gate as a child walks in.
avoid: the adult holding the child's hand inside the gate (ophalen); a child riding on an adult's shoulders (not the card); an adult pushing a pram (not the card); a child at a desk in class (not the card).
contrast: Pair with ophalen. The only difference is the direction: the adult leaves the child inside and walks off here, and takes the child's hand there.
example_nl: 's Ochtends breng ik hem weg.
example_en: In the morning I take him there.
alt: Een kind met een schooltas loopt door een open hek en een volwassene aan de straatkant zwaait.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult at the customer side of a counter pushes a plain wrapped parcel across the top with both hands flat on it, the clerk's empty hand waiting on the far side, a small arrow showing the parcel moving away from the adult.
must: both hands pushing a parcel across the counter away from the adult.
avoid: the adult taking the parcel from the clerk's hands (afhalen); an adult dropping a letter in a postbox (not the card); an adult carrying a parcel up the stairs (not the card); an adult handing a gift to a friend (aanbieden).
contrast: Pair with afhalen. The only difference is the direction: the parcel moves away from the adult here, towards the adult there.
example_nl: Ik stuur het pakket op.
alt: Een volwassene schuift een pakje over een balie naar een medewerker toe.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands at the customer side of the same counter and pulls a plain wrapped parcel towards their chest with both hands, the clerk's hands letting go of the far side, a small arrow showing the parcel moving toward the adult.
must: both hands drawing a parcel across the counter towards the adult.
avoid: the adult pushing the parcel across to the clerk (opsturen); an adult carrying a parcel through a front door (meenemen); an adult picking up a child at a gate (ophalen); an adult receiving a gift from a friend (aannemen).
contrast: Pair with opsturen. The only difference is the direction: the parcel moves towards the adult here, away from the adult there.
example_nl: Ik haal het pakket af.
alt: Een volwassene trekt met twee handen een pakje over een balie naar zich toe.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A plain round plate seen from above is completely empty and clean apart from a fork laid across it, with a few small crumb dots at the edge. An adult's hand rests on the table beside the plate.
must: a completely empty plate with a fork laid across it.
avoid: the same plate with a heap of food left on it (overlaten); a plate that has not been touched (not the card); an adult drinking from a glass (not the card); an adult washing the plate (afwassen).
contrast: Pair with overlaten. The only difference is the plate: bare and empty here, with a pile of food left on one side there.
example_nl: Ik eet alles op.
alt: Een leeg bord ligt van boven gezien op een tafel en er ligt een vork schuin op het bord.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The same plain round plate seen from above has a heap of three round vegetables and a small pile of rice pushed to one side, the other half of the plate empty, and the fork lying beside it. An adult's hand rests next to the plate.
must: a plate half empty with a heap of food pushed to one side.
avoid: the same plate completely empty (opeten); a plate heaped full and untouched (not the card); food being thrown into a bin (weggooien); a plate being passed to another person (doorgeven).
contrast: Pair with opeten. The only difference is the plate: a heap of food left on one side here, nothing left there.
example_nl: Ik laat wat groente over.
alt: Een bord van boven gezien heeft een hoopje groente en rijst aan één kant en de andere helft is leeg.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands at the sink with both hands in a basin of water topped with a few soap bubbles and holds one wet plate; a small stack of three dirty plates waits beside the basin and the plate rack is empty.
must: a plate in soapy water with bubbles beside a stack of three plates.
avoid: an adult rubbing a plate with a dry cloth beside a full rack (afdrogen); an adult scrubbing a floor with a cloth (schoonmaken); an adult filling a glass at the tap (not the card); an adult carrying a stack of plates to a table (not the card).
contrast: Pair with afdrogen. The only difference is the water: soapy hands in a basin here, a dry cloth and a full rack there.
example_nl: Ik was elke avond af.
alt: Een volwassene staat met beide handen in een bak water met zeepbellen en heeft een nat bord in de hand.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands at the same sink and rubs one plate with a plain cloth held in both hands, a plate rack beside it already holding two plates, and the basin pushed aside empty and flat. Three short shine lines mark the plate.
must: a cloth rubbing a plate beside a rack holding clean plates.
avoid: hands in soapy water with bubbles (afwassen); an adult wiping a table with a cloth (schoonmaken); an adult drying hair with a towel (not the card); an adult hanging a cloth on a hook (not the card).
contrast: Pair with afwassen. The only difference is the water: none, a dry cloth and a stocked rack here, soapy water with bubbles there.
example_nl: Ik droog de borden af.
alt: Een volwassene wrijft een bord met een doek en in het rek staan al twee borden.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands facing a friend and holds a small wrapped present with a ribbon out on two flat hands at chest height, arms stretched, the present between them, the friend's hands still down at the sides.
must: a present held out on two flat hands, the friend's hands still down.
avoid: the friend's hands closing round the present (aannemen); an adult handing a parcel across a counter (opsturen); an adult passing a loaf along a table (doorgeven); an adult tucking the present in a bag (not the card).
contrast: Pair with aannemen. The only difference is the friend's hands: still down by the sides here, closing round the present there.
example_nl: Ik bied mijn vriend een cadeau aan.
example_en: I offer my friend a present.
alt: Een volwassene houdt een ingepakt cadeautje met een lint naar voren op twee vlakke handen.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A friend stands facing an adult and closes both hands round a small wrapped present with a ribbon, the adult's flat hands still beneath it, the friend's arms bent towards the chest and the face smiling.
must: two hands closing round the present, arms bent in.
avoid: the adult holding the present out with flat hands (aanbieden); a friend pushing the present back (not the card); a friend grabbing a rope (vasthouden); a friend picking a parcel off a counter (afhalen).
contrast: Pair with aanbieden. The only difference is the friend's hands: closed round the present here, held down by the sides there.
example_nl: Ik neem het cadeau aan.
alt: Een vriend sluit beide handen om een ingepakt cadeautje en trekt het naar zich toe.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Two adults in jackets step side by side out through the open doorway towards the viewer, both over the threshold, small arrows pointing forward. The hall behind them is bare and the door stands open.
must: two walkers going out through the doorway side by side.
avoid: one adult staying in the hall and waving at the doorway (thuisblijven); an adult carrying an umbrella through the door (meenemen); an adult walking alone away from a door (weggaan); a child pulling an adult by the hand (not the card).
contrast: Pair with thuisblijven. The only difference is the second person: stepping out in a jacket beside the friend here, staying in the hall in slippers there.
example_nl: Ik ga met mijn vriend mee.
example_en: I go along with my friend.
alt: Twee volwassenen met jassen lopen naast elkaar door een open deur naar buiten.

scene: One drawing, one panel. At the same open doorway the friend in a jacket steps out over the threshold towards the viewer, a small arrow pointing forward, while the second adult stays back in the hall in slippers and house clothes, no jacket, holding a mug.
must: an adult in slippers with a mug staying in the hall as the friend steps out.
avoid: both adults in jackets stepping out together (meegaan); an adult coming home through the door (thuiskomen); an adult lying asleep in bed (uitslapen); an adult relaxing on a sofa with no doorway (not the card).
contrast: Pair with meegaan. The only difference is the second person: staying in the hall in slippers here, stepping out in a jacket beside the friend there.
example_nl: Ik blijf vandaag thuis.
example_en: I am staying at home today.
alt: Een vriend met een jas stapt over de drempel naar buiten en een volwassene op sloffen staat met een mok in de gang.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult with a shopping bag stands on the doormat at the open front door, back to the viewer, one foot across the threshold into the house, small arrows pointing into the house. The hall inside is plain.
must: one foot over the threshold, back to the viewer, arrows into the house.
avoid: an adult stepping off the doorstep towards the viewer (weggaan); an adult ringing the doorbell outside (not the card); an adult stepping off a bus (uitstappen); an adult lying in bed at home (uitslapen).
contrast: Pair with weggaan. The only difference is the direction: back turned and stepping in over the threshold here, facing out and stepping off the doorstep there.
example_nl: Ik kom om zes uur thuis.
example_en: I come home at six o'clock.
alt: Een volwassene met een boodschappentas staat met één voet over de drempel van een open voordeur.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult with a bag steps off the doorstep away from the open front door, face to the viewer, one foot already on the pavement, small arrows pointing away from the house towards the viewer. The doormat lies bare.
must: face to the viewer, stepping off the doorstep, arrows away from the house.
avoid: an adult stepping in over the threshold (thuiskomen); an adult staying on the sofa while a friend leaves (thuisblijven); a train leaving the platform (wegrijden); an adult running towards the door (not the card).
contrast: Pair with thuiskomen. The only difference is the direction: facing out and stepping off the doorstep here, back turned and stepping in over the threshold there.
example_nl: Ik ga om zeven uur weg.
alt: Een volwassene met een tas loopt bij een open voordeur vandaan, met het gezicht naar de straat.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A hand holds a lit match to the wick of a plain candle in a holder, and a small teardrop flame with three short glow lines stands on the wick. The match is tilted towards the wick and the wax below is smooth.
must: a small flame on the wick and a match tipped towards it.
avoid: the flame being blown out with smoke rising (uitblazen); a candle already burning with nobody near it (not the card); an adult switching on a lamp (aandoen); a match burning alone in a hand (not the card).
contrast: Pair with uitblazen. The only difference is the wick: a flame on it with a match here, a thin curl of smoke and no flame there.
example_nl: Ik steek de kaars aan.
alt: Een hand houdt een lucifer bij het kaarsje en er brandt een klein vlammetje.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult's face in profile on the left blows towards a plain candle in a holder with puffed cheeks and three short air lines. There is no flame: one thin wavy curl of smoke rises from the wick.
must: puffed cheeks, air lines and a thin smoke curl from the wick.
avoid: a match being held to the wick with a flame (aansteken); a candle snuffed with a cap and no breath (not the card); an adult blowing up a balloon (not the card); an adult switching off a lamp (uitdoen).
contrast: Pair with aansteken. The only difference is the wick: a thin curl of smoke after a breath here, a flame and a match there.
example_nl: Ik blaas de kaars uit.
alt: Een gezicht in profiel heeft bolle wangen bij een kaarsje en er kringelt een dun draadje rook omhoog.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A hand turns the tap handle with a small curved arrow, and a straight column of water with three splash dots runs from the spout into the basin, a ripple ring where it lands.
must: a straight water column from the spout with a ripple in the basin.
avoid: the tap with no water and a hand on the handle (dichtdraaien); a rain cloud over the basin (not the card); a bucket being poured out (not the card); a hand holding a plug over the basin (not the card).
contrast: Pair with dichtdraaien. The only difference is the spout: a water column with ripples here, a dry spout and a plain basin there.
example_nl: Ik draai de kraan open.
alt: Een hand pakt het handvat van een kraan en er stroomt een rechte straal water in de wasbak.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A hand turns the same tap handle with a small curved arrow, a single drop hangs at the end of the spout and the basin below is plain with a few leftover droplets at the bottom. No water column.
must: a dry spout with one hanging drop and a hand on the handle.
avoid: a straight water column running from the tap (opendraaien); a hand plugging the basin drain (not the card); a hand wiping a sink with a cloth (schoonmaken); a leaking tap with a drip stream (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opendraaien. The only difference is the spout: dry with one drop here, a full water column there.
example_nl: Ik draai de kraan dicht.
alt: Een hand zit op het handvat van een kraan en er glinstert nog één druppel aan de tuit.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Two hands hold a map that is folded into a small thick stack of three flat layers, the fold edges visible on both sides, a small arrow showing the sheet's sides going inward. The folded map is about the size of one hand.
must: a small thick stack of three flat layers held in two hands.
avoid: the same map spread flat and wide (uitvouwen); a map rolled into a tube (not the card); a map crumpled in a ball (weggooien); a folded shirt in a case (inpakken).
contrast: Pair with uitvouwen. The only difference is the sheet: folded into a small stack here, spread wide and flat there.
example_nl: Ik vouw de kaart op.
alt: Twee handen houden een papieren kaart vast die tot een klein dik pakketje van drie lagen is samengedrukt.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Two hands hold the same map spread wide and flat, a plain road line running across it and the fold creases forming a grid of small rectangles, arms stretched and a small arrow pointing outward on each side.
must: a wide flat sheet with grid creases and outward arrows.
avoid: the same map folded into a small stack (opvouwen); a map held crumpled in a fist (not the card); a newspaper being read (not the card); a tablecloth being laid on a table (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opvouwen. The only difference is the sheet: spread wide and flat with creases here, folded into a small stack there.
example_nl: Ik vouw de kaart uit.
alt: Twee handen houden een papieren kaart wijd en vlak open en er lopen rechte kreuken in rechthoeken overheen.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands beside a litter bin with one arm swung back and the crumpled paper ball just leaving the hand towards the bin's open top, a curved dotted path from the hand to the bin. The ground is clean.
must: a crumpled ball on a dotted arc towards the bin's open top.
avoid: an adult bending to pick the ball from the ground (oprapen); an adult handing a ball to a child (doorgeven); an adult tossing a ball into the air to play (not the card); an adult pushing a bin along the path (not the card).
contrast: Pair with oprapen. The only difference is the direction: the ball flies towards the bin here, rises from the ground into a hand there.
example_nl: Ik gooi het papier weg.
alt: Een volwassene zwaait de arm naar achteren en een prop papier vliegt in een boog naar een prullenbak.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult bends at the waist beside the same bin and picks a crumpled paper ball up off the ground with one hand, the other hand on the knee, the ball a hand's width above the ground and the bin still empty beside them.
must: a bent adult lifting a crumpled ball off the ground.
avoid: the ball flying towards the bin from a swung arm (weggooien); an adult lifting a heavy box with both hands (optillen); an adult picking apples from a tree (not the card); an adult sweeping the path with a broom (schoonmaken).
contrast: Pair with weggooien. The only difference is the direction: the ball is lifted off the ground here, thrown towards the bin there.
example_nl: Ik raap het papier op.
alt: Een gebogen volwassene pakt met één hand een prop papier van de grond.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult with bent knees and a straight back lifts a plain cardboard box clear of the floor with both hands under it, the box a hand's width above the floor and the knees still bent, a small arrow pointing upward. A plain table stands empty beside them.
must: a box a hand's width above the floor with bent knees and an upward arrow.
avoid: the box standing flat on the table with the hands letting go (neerzetten); an adult pushing a box along the floor (not the card); an adult carrying the box through a doorway (meenemen); an adult picking up a ball (oprapen).
contrast: Pair with neerzetten. The only difference is the box: a hand's width above the floor here, standing flat on the table there.
example_nl: Ik til de doos op.
alt: Een volwassene met gebogen knieën houdt een doos met beide handen een stuk boven de vloer.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands upright beside a plain table and lowers the same cardboard box until its base just meets the table top, both hands still under the box and the arms at a slight bend. A small downward arrow sits above the box.
must: a box base just touching the table with hands still under it.
avoid: the box lifted off the floor by an adult with bent knees (optillen); a glass lowered onto a table (not the card); a box dropped from height with a crash burst (not the card); a box left on a doorstep (achterlaten).
contrast: Pair with optillen. The only difference is the box: its base meeting the table here, a hand's width above the floor there.
example_nl: Ik zet de doos op tafel neer.
example_en: I put the box down on the table.
alt: Een volwassene laat een doos met beide handen zakken tot hij op een tafel staat.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult kneels on the bank and pulls the boat's rope tight round a wooden post with a final knot, the rope straight and taut between the post and the boat's front. The boat sits snug against the bank.
must: a taut rope knotted round the post and held by the adult's hands.
avoid: the rope hanging slack off the post (losbinden); an adult tying a shoelace (not the card); an adult locking a door with a key (afsluiten); an adult fastening a belt (not the card).
contrast: Pair with losbinden. The only difference is the rope: knotted tight round the post here, hanging free of it there.
example_nl: Ik bind de boot vast.
alt: Een volwassene trekt een touw met een knoop strak om een paal en de boot ligt tegen de kant.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult kneels on the bank and lifts a loop of rope off the wooden post with one hand, the rope slack and hanging in a curve, the boat drifting a short distance from the bank with a small arrow pointing away.
must: a slack rope loop lifted off the post with the boat drifting away.
avoid: the rope pulled taut round the post (vastbinden); a boat sailing alone across open water (not the card); a rope coiled on the ground (not the card); an adult cutting a rope with scissors (not the card).
contrast: Pair with vastbinden. The only difference is the rope: slack and lifted off the post here, taut and knotted round it there.
example_nl: Ik bind de boot los.
alt: Een volwassene haalt een lus touw van een paal terwijl de boot langzaam van de kant afdrijft.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Two adults sit side by side on a bench, and the nearer one turns the whole head to face the other, eyes open wide, with a short dotted line from the eyes to the other person's eyes. The second adult faces forward.
must: a turned head with a dotted line from the eyes to the other person's eyes.
avoid: the head turned away from the other person (wegkijken); both adults staring forward with no turn of the head (not the card); an adult looking through a window (not the card); an adult squinting at a map (not the card).
contrast: Pair with wegkijken. The only difference is the head: turned towards the other person with a dotted line here, turned away from them there.
example_nl: Ik kijk mijn buurman aan.
alt: Twee volwassenen zitten op een bankje en één draait het hoofd naar de ander met wijd open ogen.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Two adults sit side by side on the same bench, and the nearer one turns the whole head the other way, the chin pointing to the far edge of the picture, eyes cast away, a dotted line from the eyes towards the edge. The second adult faces forward.
must: a head turned away with a dotted line from the eyes towards the edge.
avoid: the head turned towards the other person with a dotted line (aankijken); an adult closing both eyes (not the card); an adult looking at a watch (not the card); an adult ducking behind a newspaper (not the card).
contrast: Pair with aankijken. The only difference is the head: turned away with a dotted line to the edge here, turned towards the other person there.
example_nl: Ik kijk snel weg.
alt: Twee volwassenen zitten op een bankje en één draait het gezicht naar de andere kant.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands with both arms raised high above the head, mouth closed and eyes on the child, while the child stands beside them with both arms still down by its sides, watching the adult.
must: the adult's raised arms with the child's arms still down.
avoid: the child raising its arms to match the adult (nadoen); an adult waving goodbye (not the card); an adult lifting a child (optillen); an adult explaining with a pointing stick at a board (not the card).
contrast: Pair with nadoen. The only difference is the child's arms: still down here, raised to match the adult there.
example_nl: Ik doe de beweging voor.
alt: Een volwassene houdt beide armen hoog terwijl een kind met de armen langs het lichaam toekijkt.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult stands with both arms raised high above the head, and the child beside them raises both arms too, matching the adult's pose, with a concentrated frown and eyes on the adult. Both figures now hold the same pose.
must: the child's arms raised to match the adult's raised arms.
avoid: the adult with raised arms and the child's arms still down (voordoen); a child waving at a friend (not the card); a child jumping with both arms in the air (not the card); a child hiding behind an adult (not the card).
contrast: Pair with voordoen. The only difference is the child's arms: raised to match the adult here, still down there.
example_nl: Het kind doet de juf na.
alt: Een volwassene en een kind houden allebei de armen hoog en het kind let goed op de volwassene.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A looping dotted path of small footprints curls round the chair in the corner and ends at the adult, who stands upright with both feet planted side by side and arms hanging. No footprints lie ahead of the adult.
must: a footprint trail ending at two planted feet.
avoid: the trail carrying on past a lifted foot (rondlopen); an adult running with speed lines (not the card); an adult sleeping on a chair (uitslapen); an adult standing at a door waiting (not the card).
contrast: Pair with rondlopen. The only difference is the trail: it ends at two planted feet here, it carries on past a lifted foot there.
example_nl: Ik sta even stil.
example_en: I stand still for a moment.
alt: Een stippellijn met voetafdrukken eindigt bij een volwassene die met beide voeten naast elkaar op één plek in een lege kamer blijft.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The same looping dotted path of small footprints curls round the chair and reaches the adult, who walks on with a long step, one foot lifted, and the footprints carry on ahead past the adult across the floor. The arms swing gently.
must: a footprint trail carrying on past a lifted foot.
avoid: the trail ending at two planted feet (stilstaan); an adult running in a straight line (not the card); an adult walking out through a door (weggaan); an adult stepping on a bus (instappen).
contrast: Pair with stilstaan. The only difference is the trail: it carries on past a lifted foot here, it ends at two planted feet there.
example_nl: Ik loop in de kamer rond.
example_en: I walk around in the room.
alt: Een volwassene zet een grote stap en achter de voeten kronkelt een stippellijn met voetafdrukken door de kamer.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult leans over a thick open dictionary on the table with one finger running down a column of plain wavy lines, the head tilted and the eyes on the page. The notepad lies untouched on the right with its page blank.
must: a finger running down a column in a thick open book.
avoid: the hand writing in the notepad with a pen (opschrijven); an adult reading a newspaper (not the card); an adult visiting a friend at a front door (not this sense); an adult pointing at a map (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opschrijven. The only difference is the hand: a finger on the open book here, a pen on the notepad there.
example_nl: Ik zoek het woord op.
alt: Een volwassene laat een vinger langs een kolom in een dik opengeslagen boek lopen.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult sits at the same table with the pen in the right hand, writing wavy lines on the notepad with the page half filled, the head tilted over the pad. The thick book lies closed to the left.
must: a pen with wavy lines appearing on the notepad beside a closed book.
avoid: a finger running down the open book (opzoeken); an adult drawing a picture on the pad (not the card); an adult typing on a laptop (not the card); an adult reading a letter aloud (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opzoeken. The only difference is the hand: a pen on the notepad here, a finger on the open book there.
example_nl: Ik schrijf het woord op.
alt: Een volwassene trekt met een pen golvende regels op een blok naast een dichtgeslagen boek.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A teacher stands in front of a desk with a stack of paper sheets in one hand and holds one sheet out to a student at the side desk, the student's hand just reaching up for it, a small arrow from the teacher towards the student.
must: a sheet held out from the teacher's stack towards a reaching student.
avoid: a student putting a sheet down on the teacher's desk (inleveren); a teacher writing on a board (not the card); a person passing a loaf along a table (doorgeven); a teacher holding a wrapped present out (aanbieden).
contrast: Pair with inleveren. The only difference is the direction: sheets move from the teacher to the student here, from the student to the teacher's desk there.
example_nl: Ik deel de toets uit.
alt: Een volwassene bij een bureau geeft een vel papier aan een leerling die zijn hand opsteekt.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A student stands at the teacher's desk and lays one paper sheet on top of a small stack already lying there, the teacher seated behind it with a pen, a small arrow from the student towards the desk.
must: a sheet laid down on a stack on the teacher's desk.
avoid: a teacher holding a sheet out to a student (uitdelen); a student writing at a desk (not the card); a student throwing a sheet in a bin (weggooien); a student posting a letter (opsturen).
contrast: Pair with uitdelen. The only difference is the direction: the sheet moves from the student to the teacher's desk here, from the teacher to the student there.
example_nl: Ik lever de toets in.
alt: Een leerling legt een vel papier op een stapeltje op het bureau van een leraar die met een pen zit.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A hand pushes the plug on a cable into a wall socket until it is flush, the cable running in a straight line from the open laptop on the table to the socket; three short charge lines beside the laptop's corner show it receives power.
must: a plug flush in the wall socket with the cable running straight to the laptop.
avoid: the plug pulled out and lying apart from the socket (loskoppelen); a lamp being lit (aandoen); a radio playing with sound lines (aanzetten); a hand tying a rope (vastbinden).
contrast: Pair with loskoppelen. The only difference is the plug: pushed flush into the socket here, drawn out and apart from it there.
example_nl: Ik sluit de laptop aan.
alt: Een hand duwt een stekker in een stopcontact en de kabel loopt strak naar een open laptop.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A hand pulls the plug of the cable out of the wall socket, the plug a clear hand's width from the socket and the cable curving loose in the air, a small arrow pointing away from the wall; the open laptop sits on the table with no charge lines.
must: a plug a hand's width from the socket with the cable loose in the air.
avoid: the plug pushed flush into the socket (aansluiten); a hand pulling a tooth (not the card); a radio switched off with no sound lines (uitzetten); a tap turned off (dichtdraaien).
contrast: Pair with aansluiten. The only difference is the plug: drawn out from the socket here, pushed flush into it there.
example_nl: Ik koppel de laptop los.
alt: Een hand trekt een stekker uit het stopcontact en de kabel zwaait vrij door de lucht.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A plain vase with a flower leans at a steep angle in the middle of the table, tipping over onto its side by itself, three short motion lines beside it and a few drops spilling from the opening; nobody stands near and the table is otherwise bare.
must: a steeply tilted vase tipping alone with nobody beside it.
avoid: the same vase knocked by an elbow (omgooien); a vase standing upright (not the card); a vase lying broken on the floor (not the card); a flower pulled from the vase by a hand (not the card).
contrast: Pair with omgooien. The only difference is the cause: nothing touches the vase here, an elbow hits it there.
example_nl: De vaas valt om.
alt: Een vaas met een bloem helt midden op een tafel sterk opzij en er is niemand in de buurt.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult's elbow swings out and hits a plain vase with a flower in the middle of the table, the vase tilting onto its side at a steep angle with three short motion lines and a few drops from the opening; the adult, startled with wide eyes, looks at the vase.
must: an adult's elbow touching the tipping vase.
avoid: the vase tipping alone with nobody near (omvallen); a vase set down carefully by hand (neerzetten); an adult carrying a vase (optillen); an adult dropping a plate on the floor (not the card).
contrast: Pair with omvallen. The only difference is the cause: an elbow hits the vase here, nothing touches it there.
example_nl: Ik gooi de vaas om.
alt: Een elleboog raakt een vaas midden op een tafel en een volwassene kijkt geschrokken naar de vaas.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Three seated adults in a row at a table, and the left one hands a bread board with a loaf to the middle one, whose hands are just taking the board, the right-hand adult's hands resting open on the table, a small arrow along the row.
must: a loaf on a board travelling from the left hand to the middle one.
avoid: the loaf held still in a single pair of hands (vasthouden); a loaf being offered as a present with flat hands (aanbieden); a loaf thrown into the air (weggooien); a loaf being sliced with a knife (not the card).
contrast: Pair with vasthouden. The only difference is the loaf: it moves on to the next person's hands here, it stays in one person's grip there.
example_nl: Ik geef het brood door.
alt: Drie volwassenen zitten aan een tafel en de eerste reikt een broodplank met een brood naar de tweede.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Three seated adults in a row at a table, and the middle one grips the bread board with the loaf in both hands against the chest, knuckles tight, while the other two sit with hands resting on the table and look at the loaf. No arrow along the row.
must: two tight hands gripping the loaf at the chest with no arrow along the row.
avoid: the loaf moving along the row with a small arrow (doorgeven); a loaf held out on flat hands (aanbieden); a hand grabbing a rope on a boat (vastbinden); a loaf lying alone on the table (not the card).
contrast: Pair with doorgeven. The only difference is the loaf: gripped tight in one pair of hands here, moving on to the next hands there.
example_nl: Ik houd het brood vast.
example_en: I hold on to the bread.
alt: Drie volwassenen zitten aan een tafel en de middelste drukt een brood op een plank met beide handen tegen zich aan.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult sits upright at the desk with both hands on the laptop keys and a straight back, the lamp on and a stack of papers at the elbow. The window behind is dark with a moon, the second desk's chair stands empty, and the armchair is empty.
must: an upright adult typing beside an empty desk under a night window.
avoid: an adult lying back in the armchair with the laptop closed (uitrusten); an adult stretching at the desk (not the card); an adult taking a laptop to a car (meenemen); an adult sleeping on the desk (not the card).
contrast: Pair with uitrusten. The only difference is the posture: upright at the desk typing here, leaning back in the armchair there.
example_nl: Ik werk vanavond door.
alt: Een volwassene zit 's avonds rechtop aan een bureau en typt op een laptop terwijl het bureau ernaast leeg is.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult leans back in the armchair beside the desk with both hands behind the head and feet up on a stool, eyes closed and a calm small smile, the laptop shut on the desk and a soft curved line of breath rising from the face.
must: a leaning-back adult with closed eyes and the laptop shut.
avoid: an adult upright at the desk typing (doorwerken); an adult asleep in bed (uitslapen); an adult jumping or exercising (not the card); an adult relaxing in an armchair while another walks out (thuisblijven).
contrast: Pair with doorwerken. The only difference is the posture: leaning back in the armchair with the laptop shut here, upright at the desk typing there.
example_nl: Ik rust even uit.
alt: Een volwassene leunt met gesloten ogen achterover in een leunstoel en de laptop op het bureau is dicht.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A child stands on tiptoe on the mat under the bar of a climbing frame, and both hands are just closing round the bar, fingers curling over it, arms stretched straight up. A small arrow points up at the hands. Both feet are still on the mat.
must: two hands curling shut round the bar above a child on tiptoe.
avoid: the hands opening with the child dropping to the mat (loslaten); a child hanging still with both hands round the bar (vasthouden); a child lifting a box from the floor (optillen); a hand snatching at a rail (grijpen); a child climbing a ladder (not the card).
contrast: Pair with loslaten. The only difference is the hands: closing round the bar here, opening below it there.
example_nl: Ik pak de stang stevig vast.
alt: Een kind staat op de tenen onder een stang van een klimrek en de vingers krullen om de stang.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A child under the bar of the same climbing frame has just opened both hands, fingers spread a hand's width below the bar, and drops towards the mat with knees bent. A small arrow points down from the hands. The feet are a little above the mat.
must: two open hands just below the bar and a child dropping to the mat.
avoid: hands closing round the bar on tiptoe (vastpakken); a child hanging still from the bar (vasthouden); a child falling off a bike (not the card); a box being set down (neerzetten).
contrast: Pair with vastpakken. The only difference is the hands: opening below the bar here, closing round it there.
example_nl: Ik laat de stang voorzichtig los.
example_en: I carefully let go of the bar.
alt: Een kind spreidt de vingers onder de stang van een klimrek en zakt met gebogen knieën naar de mat.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult at a table writes in an empty box on a sheet, the pen tip in the box and three short greeked strokes already inside it; the boxes above are filled with strokes and the boxes below are still empty. No line runs through any strokes.
must: a pen tip inside a box with fresh strokes and empty boxes below.
avoid: a straight line drawn through a row of strokes (doorstrepen); a pen writing in a notebook (opschrijven); a sheet handed to a teacher (inleveren); a sheet coming out of a printer (afdrukken).
contrast: Pair with doorstrepen. The only difference is the pen: adding strokes inside an empty box here, drawing one line through finished strokes there.
example_nl: Ik vul het formulier helemaal in.
example_en: I fill in the whole form.
alt: Een volwassene zet met een pen krabbels in een leeg vakje op een vel met een kolom vakjes.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult at the same table holds the pen at the end of one straight line drawn right through a row of greeked strokes in a filled box, the line reaching past both ends of the strokes. The boxes above keep their strokes and the boxes below are still empty.
must: one straight line running through a row of strokes, the pen at its end.
avoid: a pen adding strokes to an empty box (invullen); a sheet torn in two (not the card); a pen writing in a notebook (opschrijven); a sheet crumpled into a ball (weggooien).
contrast: Pair with invullen. The only difference is the pen: drawing one line through finished strokes here, adding strokes to an empty box there.
example_nl: Ik streep een fout snel door.
example_en: I quickly cross out a mistake.
alt: Een volwassene trekt met een pen een rechte lijn dwars over een rij krabbels in een vakje.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A dog on the lawn runs to the right, away from the adult at the left edge, its back to the adult and its tail out behind; a small arrow points right. The adult stands upright with one arm stretched towards the dog and the mouth open.
must: a dog running off to the right with its back to the adult.
avoid: the dog running towards a crouching adult (terugkomen); a dog walking calmly on a lead (not the card); an adult walking out of a front door (weggaan); a dog lying asleep (not the card).
contrast: Pair with terugkomen. The only difference is the dog: running away from the adult here, running back to the adult there.
example_nl: Onze hond loopt steeds weg.
alt: Een hond rent over het gras naar rechts, met de rug naar een volwassene die een arm uitstrekt.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The same dog on the lawn runs to the left, towards the adult at the left edge, its face to the adult and its ears flying; a small arrow points left. The adult crouches with both hands open to meet the dog.
must: a dog running towards a crouching adult with open hands.
avoid: the dog running off with its back to the adult (weglopen); an adult arriving at a front door (thuiskomen); a dog sitting beside the adult (not the card); a train pulling into a station (aankomen).
contrast: Pair with weglopen. The only difference is the dog: running back to the adult here, running away from the adult there.
example_nl: Onze hond komt altijd snel terug.
example_en: Our dog always comes back quickly.
alt: Een hond rent over het gras naar een volwassene die gehurkt met open handen wacht.

scene: SKIP: sunrise and sunset as stills differ only in the arrow (the sun sits half on the horizon in both), any cue that tells them apart (a moon, a dark sky) is a second change, and the half sun at the edge is the Vaste uitdrukkingen 's ochtends picture.
must: a half sun on the horizon with a bold arrow pointing up.
avoid: the same half sun with the arrow pointing down (ondergaan); a full sun high in an empty sky (not the card); a table lamp with rays (aandoen); a balloon rising (not the card).
contrast: Pair with ondergaan. The only difference is the arrow beside the sun: pointing up here, pointing down there.
example_nl: De zon komt vandaag vroeg op.
alt: Een halve zon staat op de horizon boven een vlak veld en een pijl ernaast wijst omhoog.

scene: SKIP: set with opkomen, for the reason given there; the slug is also the Werkwoorden row ondergaan (to undergo, inseparable, heeft ondergaan).
must: a half sun on the horizon with a bold arrow pointing down.
avoid: the same half sun with the arrow pointing up (opkomen); a moon in a dark sky (not the card); a table lamp with no rays (uitdoen); a ball dropping (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opkomen. The only difference is the arrow beside the sun: pointing down here, pointing up there.
example_nl: De zon gaat vandaag laat onder.
alt: Een halve zon staat op de horizon boven een vlak veld en een pijl ernaast wijst omlaag.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A plain printer on a desk pushes a sheet with greeked strokes half out of the front slot into the tray, two short motion lines beside it and a small arrow pointing out. The glass lid on top is shut and an adult's hand waits by the tray.
must: a sheet sliding half out of the front slot with an outward arrow.
avoid: a sheet laid face down on the glass under the raised lid (inscannen); a sheet being written on with a pen (invullen); a cable pulled from a laptop (loskoppelen); a parcel handed over a counter (opsturen).
contrast: Pair with inscannen. The only difference is the sheet: sliding out of the front here, lying on the glass under the lid there.
example_nl: Ik druk de brief even af.
alt: Uit de voorkant van een printer schuift een vel met krabbels naar de bak.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult raises the glass lid of the same printer with one hand and with the other lays a sheet with greeked strokes face down on the glass, a small arrow pointing down onto it. The front slot and tray are empty.
must: a sheet laid face down on the glass under a raised lid.
avoid: a sheet sliding out of the front slot (afdrukken); a letter put into an envelope (opsturen); the lid of a box being lifted (optillen); a photo taken with a phone (not the card).
contrast: Pair with afdrukken. The only difference is the sheet: laid on the glass under the lid here, sliding out of the front there.
example_nl: Ik scan mijn paspoort even in.
alt: Een volwassene houdt de klep van een printer omhoog en legt een vel omgekeerd op het glas.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A small bird sits on the perch inside a round cage on a table, and an adult's hand pushes the small cage door shut, the door a finger's width from the frame with a small curved arrow. The open window behind is empty.
must: a hand pushing the cage door shut on a bird inside.
avoid: the bird flying out of the open door (vrijlaten); a hand locking a front door with a key (afsluiten); a bird sitting on a branch outside (not the card); a lid closing on a box (not the card).
contrast: Pair with vrijlaten. The only difference is the bird and its door: bird inside as the door shuts here, bird flying out of the open door there.
example_nl: Ik sluit de vogel 's nachts op.
example_en: I shut the bird in at night.
alt: Een hand duwt het deurtje van een vogelkooi dicht terwijl een vogeltje binnen op een stokje zit.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult's hand holds the small door of the same round cage wide open, and the bird flies out through it towards the open window, wings spread, a small arrow ahead of it. The perch inside the cage is empty.
must: a bird with spread wings leaving the open cage door.
avoid: the bird inside as a hand pushes the door shut (opsluiten); a bird flying high over a field (not the card); an adult opening a front door (opendoen); a hand opening a cage door with no bird (openen); a child dropping from a bar (loslaten).
contrast: Pair with opsluiten. The only difference is the bird and its door: bird flying out of the open door here, bird inside as the door shuts there.
example_nl: Ik laat de vogel buiten vrij.
example_en: I let the bird go outside.
alt: Een hand houdt het deurtje van een vogelkooi wijd open en een vogeltje vliegt eruit naar het raam.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult pushes the second pole of a small ridge tent upright, and the tent cloth rises over it into a taut triangle, a small arrow pointing up. The empty tent bag lies on the grass and two pegs are already in the ground.
must: the tent cloth rising into a taut triangle over a pole with an upward arrow.
avoid: the tent cloth sinking flat as a pole is drawn out (afbreken); a market stall being built (not the card); a person lifting a box (optillen); a finished tent with nobody near it (not the card).
contrast: Pair with afbreken. The only difference is the tent: rising taut over the pole here, sinking flat as the pole comes out there.
example_nl: Ik zet de tent snel op.
example_en: I put up the tent quickly.
alt: Een volwassene duwt een stok rechtop en het tentdoek komt strak te staan.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult draws the second pole out of the same small tent, and the tent cloth sags and folds towards the grass, a small arrow pointing down. The empty tent bag lies open beside it and two pegs lie loose on the grass.
must: the tent cloth sagging to the grass as a pole is drawn out with a downward arrow.
avoid: the tent cloth rising taut over a pole (opzetten); a person snapping a stick in two (not the card); a map being folded (opvouwen); a person packing a suitcase (inpakken).
contrast: Pair with opzetten. The only difference is the tent: sinking flat as the pole comes out here, rising taut over the pole there.
example_nl: Ik breek de tent morgen af.
example_en: I'll take the tent down tomorrow.
alt: Een volwassene haalt een stok uit een kleine tent en het doek zakt naar het gras.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A player in kit steps over the side line onto the pitch, one foot on the grass inside the line and the other still outside, arms swinging and eyes on the ball; a small arrow points onto the pitch. The bench behind is empty.
must: one foot crossing the side line onto the pitch beside an empty bench.
avoid: the player sitting on the bench watching (toekijken); a person tripping and falling (not the card); a person stepping off a bus (uitstappen); two players kicking the ball (not the card).
contrast: Pair with toekijken. The only difference is the player: stepping onto the pitch here, sitting on the bench there.
example_nl: In de tweede helft val ik in.
example_en: I come on as a substitute in the second half.
alt: Een speler zet een voet over de zijlijn op het gras terwijl de bank erachter leeg is.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The same player in kit sits on the low bench outside the side line, hands on the knees, head turned to follow the ball on the pitch; both feet are flat on the grass outside the line. A dotted sight line runs from the eyes to the ball.
must: a seated player on the bench with a sight line to the ball.
avoid: the player stepping over the side line (invallen); a person looking away from someone (wegkijken); a person resting in an armchair (uitrusten); a crowd cheering in a stand (aanmoedigen).
contrast: Pair with invallen. The only difference is the player: sitting on the bench here, stepping onto the pitch there.
example_nl: Vandaag kijk ik alleen maar toe.
alt: Een speler zit op een bank naast het veld en volgt met zijn ogen de bal.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The low garden gate stands wide open. An adult stands square in the gap, legs apart, leaning forward with one hand flat on the chest of the dog, which pushes forward with its front paws on the path outside and cannot pass.
must: an adult filling the open gap with a hand on the dog's chest.
avoid: the adult stepped aside with the dog trotting through (doorlaten); a dog barking at a gate (blaffen); a person tying a dog to a post (vastbinden); a dog running off across a lawn (weglopen); a hand pushing a cage door shut (opsluiten).
contrast: Pair with doorlaten. The only difference is the adult: standing in the open gap and stopping the dog here, stepped aside to let it pass there.
example_nl: Ik houd de hond bij het hek tegen.
example_en: I hold the dog back at the gate.
alt: Een volwassene staat wijdbeens in een open tuinhek met een hand op de borst van een hond die naar voren duwt.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The same low garden gate stands wide open. The adult has stepped aside out of the gap, back against the fence and one arm sweeping towards the path, and the dog trots through the gap onto the path inside, a small arrow along its way.
must: a dog trotting through the open gap past an adult standing aside.
avoid: the adult in the gap with a hand on the dog's chest (tegenhouden); an adult opening a front door (opendoen); a person walking a dog on a lead (not the card); a bird flying out of a cage (vrijlaten).
contrast: Pair with tegenhouden. The only difference is the adult: stepped aside to let the dog pass here, standing in the open gap and stopping it there.
example_nl: Bij het hek laat ik de hond door.
example_en: At the gate I let the dog through.
alt: Een volwassene staat opzij naast het hek en een hond draaft langs hem naar het huis.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Three adults sit at a square table. The standing adult pushes the fourth chair in at the empty side, its seat already tucked under the table edge and both hands on its back; a small arrow points in towards the table. The stack against the wall stays short.
must: a fourth chair tucked in under the table edge at the empty side.
avoid: the fourth chair carried away towards the stack at the wall (weghalen); a person sitting down on a chair (not the card); a box put down on the floor (neerzetten); plates set out on a table (klaarzetten).
contrast: Pair with weghalen. The only difference is the fourth chair: tucked in at the table here, carried off towards the stack at the wall there.
example_nl: Ik zet de stoel netjes terug.
example_en: I put the chair back neatly.
alt: Een volwassene schuift een vierde stoel onder de rand van een tafel waar drie mensen zitten.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Three adults sit at the same square table, the fourth side bare. The standing adult carries the fourth chair, lifted off the floor, a step from the table towards the short stack of chairs against the wall at the right; a small arrow points to the stack.
must: a fourth chair carried off the floor towards the stack at the wall.
avoid: the fourth chair tucked in at the table (terugzetten); a person getting up from a chair (opstaan); a box lifted from the floor (optillen); a person tidying toys into a box (opruimen).
contrast: Pair with terugzetten. The only difference is the fourth chair: carried off towards the stack at the wall here, tucked in at the table there.
example_nl: Ik haal die oude stoel weg.
example_en: I take that old chair away.
alt: Een volwassene draagt een vierde stoel van de tafel naar een stapel stoelen tegen de muur.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A hand holds a small spoon heaped with sugar above a cup of coffee and tips it, so a stream of grains falls into the coffee; a small arrow points down into the cup. The sugar bowl beside the cup stands open.
must: a tipped spoon pouring a stream of sugar grains into the cup.
avoid: the spoon circling inside the coffee (omroeren); a jug pouring milk into a glass (not the card); a hand blowing on a hot cup (not the card); a cup offered to someone (aanbieden).
contrast: Pair with omroeren. The only difference is the spoon: tipping sugar into the cup here, circling inside the coffee there.
example_nl: Ik voeg een schepje suiker toe.
example_en: I add a spoonful of sugar.
alt: Een hand houdt een lepeltje schuin boven een kop koffie en er valt suiker in de kop.

scene: One drawing, one panel. A hand holds a small spoon upright in the same cup of coffee and moves it round, with two curved swirl lines on the surface and a small circular arrow above the cup. The sugar bowl beside the cup has its lid on.
must: a spoon upright in the cup with swirl lines and a circular arrow.
avoid: a tipped spoon pouring sugar into the cup (toevoegen); a hand turning a tap (opendraaien); a hand washing a cup (afwassen); a person drinking from the cup (not the card).
contrast: Pair with toevoegen. The only difference is the spoon: circling inside the coffee here, tipping sugar into the cup there.
example_nl: Ik roer de koffie even om.
example_en: I give the coffee a stir.
alt: Een hand beweegt een lepeltje in kringetjes door een kop koffie en er komen golfjes op het oppervlak.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult seen from the side rests one hand flat on the chest, and the chest swells high under it; a small arrow at the hand points into the chest. Two short curved lines lead into the nostrils. The mouth is closed and the cheeks are flat.
must: a hand on a swelling chest with a small arrow pointing in.
avoid: fingers pinching the nose with no arrow (inhouden); a hand on a sinking chest with an arrow out (uitademen); a person blowing out a candle (uitblazen); a person smelling a flower (not the card).
contrast: Pair with inhouden and uitademen. The only difference is the arrow at the chest: pointing in here, absent or pointing out there.
example_nl: Ik adem rustig door mijn neus in.
example_en: I breathe in calmly through my nose.
alt: Een volwassene met een hand op een rijzende borst zuigt lucht door de neus naar binnen.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult seen from the side rests one hand flat on a high, still chest and pinches the nose shut with two fingers of the other hand; the mouth is pressed shut, the cheeks flat, and no arrow or line shows anywhere.
must: fingers pinching the nose and a hand on a still chest with no arrow.
avoid: a hand on a swelling chest with an arrow in (inademen); a hand on a sinking chest with an arrow out (uitademen); a person filling an air mattress by mouth (blazen); a person with a hand over the mouth (not the card).
contrast: Pair with inademen and uitademen. The only difference is the arrow at the chest: absent here, pointing in or out there.
example_nl: Ik houd mijn adem even in.
example_en: I hold my breath for a moment.
alt: Een volwassene knijpt met twee vingers in de neus en heeft een hand op een roerloze borst.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult seen from the side rests one hand flat on the chest, and the chest sinks low under it; a small arrow at the hand points out of the chest. The mouth hangs slack and open with no pursed lips, and two short lines leave it.
must: a hand on a sinking chest with a small arrow pointing out.
avoid: a hand on a swelling chest with an arrow in (inademen); fingers pinching the nose (inhouden); a person blowing out a candle (uitblazen); a person yawning (not the card).
contrast: Pair with inademen and inhouden. The only difference is the arrow at the chest: pointing out here, pointing in or absent there.
example_nl: Ik adem langzaam door mijn mond uit.
example_en: I breathe out slowly through my mouth.
alt: Een volwassene met een hand op een zakkende borst duwt lucht door de slappe, open mond naar buiten.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The left child grabs the teddy bear out of the hands of the right child and pulls it towards their own chest, a small arrow pointing left; the hands of the right child stay open and empty and the mouth is open in protest.
must: a teddy bear pulled from open hands towards the chest of the left child.
avoid: the teddy bear held out back to the right child (teruggeven); a book slid back across a library counter (terugbrengen); a child picking a toy up from the floor (oprapen); a parcel handed over a counter (afhalen).
contrast: Pair with teruggeven. The only difference is the teddy bear: pulled away from the right child here, held out back to the right child there.
example_nl: Ik pak de knuffel van mijn broer af.
example_en: I take the teddy away from my brother.
alt: Een kind trekt een knuffelbeer uit de handen van een ander kind naar de eigen borst.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The left child holds the teddy bear out in both open hands towards the right child, a small arrow pointing right; the right child still has both arms stretched out from the snatch and an upset face, the mouth turned down.
must: a teddy bear held out on open hands towards the other child.
avoid: the teddy bear pulled away from the right child (afpakken); a book slid back to a librarian (terugbrengen); a gift offered across a table (aanbieden); bread passed along a row (doorgeven).
contrast: Pair with afpakken. The only difference is the teddy bear: held out back to the right child here, pulled away from the right child there.
example_nl: Ik geef de knuffel aan mijn broer terug.
example_en: I give the teddy back to my brother.
alt: Een kind reikt een knuffelbeer op open handen aan een ander kind dat nog boos kijkt.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The flaps of a waist-high ticket gate stand open and an adult walks through them from the hall towards the platform, face to the train, one foot past the flaps; a small arrow points right towards the train. A plain card hangs lowered in one hand, away from the reader.
must: an adult stepping through the open gate flaps towards the train.
avoid: the adult stepping through the flaps away from the train (uitchecken); a bank card held to a card terminal (pinnen); a person stepping into a bus (instappen); a person paying at a shop till (betalen); a person showing a ticket to a guard (not the card).
contrast: Pair with uitchecken. The only difference is the way through the open flaps: towards the train here, away from it there.
example_nl: Bij het poortje check ik in.
example_en: I check in at the gate.
