alt: Een volwassene loopt door de open klepjes van een poortje naar het perron met de trein.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The flaps of the same ticket gate stand open and the adult walks through them from the platform towards the hall, back to the train, one foot past the flaps; a small arrow points left towards the hall. A plain card hangs lowered in one hand, away from the reader.
must: an adult stepping through the open gate flaps away from the train.
avoid: the adult stepping through the flaps towards the train (inchecken); a bank card held to a card terminal (pinnen); a person getting off a bus (uitstappen); a train arriving at a platform (aankomen); an adult walking out of a front door (weggaan).
contrast: Pair with inchecken. The only difference is the way through the open flaps: away from the train here, towards it there.
example_nl: Op het station check ik uit.
example_en: I check out at the station.
alt: Een volwassene loopt met de rug naar de trein door de open klepjes van een poortje naar de hal.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult in the driver's seat pulls the seat belt across the chest and clicks it into the clip beside the hip, a small arrow pointing into the clip. The belt is the mark: a broad band lying flat and tight from shoulder to hip.
must: a broad belt lying tight across the chest from shoulder to hip.
avoid: the belt hanging loose by the door (losmaken); a person putting on a coat (aantrekken); a rope tied round a post (vastbinden); a person stepping into a bus (instappen).
contrast: Pair with losmaken. The only difference is the belt: tight across the chest here, hanging loose by the door there.
example_nl: In de auto doe ik mijn gordel om.
example_en: In the car I put on my seat belt.
alt: Een volwassene in een auto heeft de autogordel strak over de borst en klikt hem in de sluiting.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult in the driver's seat has just pressed the clip beside the hip, and the belt is the mark: a broad band hanging loose and slack beside the door pillar, off the chest, a small arrow pointing away from the clip.
must: a broad belt hanging loose by the door, off the chest.
avoid: the belt tight across the chest (omdoen); a person untying a rope from a post (losbinden); a cable pulled from a laptop (loskoppelen); a person taking off a coat (uittrekken).
contrast: Pair with omdoen. The only difference is the belt: hanging loose by the door here, tight across the chest there.
example_nl: Bij aankomst maak ik mijn gordel los.
example_en: On arrival I undo my seat belt.
alt: Een volwassene in een auto drukt op de sluiting en de autogordel hangt slap naast de deur.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The librarian behind the counter starts to slide a closed book towards the visitor, the book still at the near edge under the flat hand of the librarian; a small arrow points right, towards the visitor. A short stack of books stands at the elbow of the librarian.
must: a book under the hand of the librarian at the near edge, arrow to the visitor.
avoid: the visitor sliding the book back across the counter (terugbrengen); a teddy bear held out back to a child (teruggeven); a parcel handed over at a post counter (afhalen); a gift offered in both hands (aanbieden).
contrast: Pair with terugbrengen. The only difference is the direction of the book: from the librarian to the visitor here, from the visitor to the librarian there.
example_nl: De bibliotheek leent ook tijdschriften uit.
example_en: The library also lends out magazines.
alt: Een bibliothecaris heeft de hand op een gesloten boek en schuift het naar een bezoeker.

scene: One drawing, one panel. The visitor in front of the counter starts to slide a closed book towards the librarian, the book still at the visitor's edge under the flat hand of the visitor; a small arrow points left, towards the librarian. The stack of books at the elbow of the librarian is unchanged.
must: a book under the hand of the visitor at the far edge, arrow to the librarian.
avoid: the librarian pushing the book to the visitor (uitlenen); a teddy bear held out back to a child (teruggeven); homework handed in to a teacher (inleveren); a person posting a parcel (opsturen).
contrast: Pair with uitlenen. The only difference is the direction of the book: from the visitor to the librarian here, from the librarian to the visitor there.
example_nl: Ik breng het boek op tijd terug.
example_en: I bring the book back on time.
alt: Een bezoeker heeft de hand op een gesloten boek op de balie en schuift het naar de bibliothecaris.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult at the table sets the last of four clean plates down in front of an empty chair, three plates and three cups already in place round the table; a small arrow points down to the table. The cupboard door behind is open.
must: the last clean plate going down into a row of laid places.
avoid: a stack of used plates lifted off the table (afruimen); a chair tucked in at the table (terugzetten); a plate lowered in front of a guest (serveren); plates washed at a sink (afwassen).
contrast: Pair with afruimen. The only difference is the plates: going down onto the table here, coming off it in a stack there.
example_nl: Ik zet de borden alvast klaar.
example_en: I set out the plates in advance.
alt: Een volwassene legt een schoon bord op een tafel waar al drie borden en drie kopjes staan.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult at the same table lifts a stack of four used plates with crumbs and a cup on top off the table, the places bare round it; a small arrow points up from the table. The cupboard door behind is open.
must: a stack of used plates lifted off a bare table.
avoid: a clean plate set down into a laid place (klaarzetten); toys tidied into a box (opruimen); a chair carried away from the table (weghalen); a table wiped with a cloth (schoonmaken).
contrast: Pair with klaarzetten. The only difference is the plates: coming off the table in a stack here, going down onto it there.
example_nl: Na het eten ruim ik de tafel af.
example_en: After the meal I clear the table.
alt: Een volwassene pakt een stapel vuile borden met kruimels van een lege tafel.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult crouches at an open dishwasher and holds a stack of dirty plates in the crook of one arm and lowers the top one into an empty slot of the pulled-out rack, a small arrow pointing down into the slot. The rack is half full.
must: a dirty plate lowered into a slot of the pulled-out rack.
avoid: a clean plate lifted out of the rack (uitruimen); plates washed by hand in a sink (afwassen); a plate dried with a towel (afdrogen); boxes loaded into a van (inladen).
contrast: Pair with uitruimen. The only difference is the plate: going down into the rack here, coming up out of it there.
example_nl: Na het eten ruim ik de vaatwasser in.
example_en: After dinner I load the dishwasher.
alt: Een volwassene met een stapel vuile borden op de arm zet een bord in het rek van een open vaatwasser.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult crouches at the same open dishwasher and holds a stack of clean, shining plates in the crook of one arm and lifts one more up out of a slot of the pulled-out rack, a small arrow pointing up out of the slot. The rack is half full.
must: a clean shining plate lifted up out of the rack.
avoid: a dirty plate lowered into the rack (inruimen); a plate dried with a towel (afdrogen); boxes lifted out of a van (uitladen); things taken out of a suitcase (uitpakken).
contrast: Pair with inruimen. The only difference is the plate: coming up out of the rack here, going down into it there.
example_nl: Elke ochtend ruim ik de vaatwasser uit.
example_en: Every morning I unload the dishwasher.
alt: Een volwassene met een stapel schone borden op de arm haalt een glanzend bord uit het rek van een open vaatwasser.

scene: SKIP: getting on and getting off a bike pass through the same poses, so the two stills differ only in the arrow, and any honest cue (which foot is down, the lean of the bike, the rider rising or sinking) changes more than one element.
must: a leg swinging up over the saddle with the other foot still on the ground.
avoid: a leg coming back down over the saddle to the ground (afstappen); a person stepping into a bus (instappen); a person riding fast (not the card); a person standing still on a pavement (stilstaan).
contrast: Pair with afstappen. The only difference is the swinging leg: going up over the saddle onto the bike here, coming back down over it to the ground there.
example_nl: Na het stoplicht stap ik weer op.
example_en: After the traffic light I get back on.
alt: Een volwassene heeft de handen aan het stuur van een fiets en zwaait een been over het zadel.

scene: SKIP: set with opstappen, for the reason given there.
must: a leg coming back down over the saddle towards the ground.
avoid: a leg swinging up over the saddle onto the bike (opstappen); a person getting off a bus (uitstappen); a child dropping from a bar (loslaten); a person falling off a bike (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opstappen. The only difference is the swinging leg: coming back down over the saddle to the ground here, going up over it onto the bike there.
example_nl: Bij de brug stap ik af.
example_en: At the bridge I get off.
alt: Een volwassene laat een been over het zadel van een fiets naar de grond zakken.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult in a plain jacket pulls the zip pull up to the chin with one hand, the jacket closed from the waist to the neck, the other hand holding the bottom of the zip; a small arrow points up along the zip.
must: a zip pull drawn up to the chin over a closed jacket front.
avoid: the zip pull drawn down with the jacket opening (openritsen); a coat being put on over the shoulders (aantrekken); a bag being packed (inpakken); a seat belt clicked into its clip (omdoen).
contrast: Pair with openritsen. The only difference is the zip: pulled up to the chin with the jacket closed here, pulled down with the jacket opening there.
example_nl: Buiten rits ik mijn jas dicht.
example_en: Outside I zip up my coat.
alt: Een volwassene trekt het lipje van een jas omhoog tot onder de kin.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult in the same plain jacket pulls the zip pull down towards the waist, the two halves of the jacket parting above it to show a plain shirt; a small arrow points down along the zip. The other hand holds the edge of the jacket.
must: a zip pull drawn down with the jacket halves parting above it.
avoid: the zip pull drawn up to the chin (dichtritsen); a coat being taken off at the elbows (uittrekken); a suitcase being unpacked (uitpakken); a door swung wide (opendoen).
contrast: Pair with dichtritsen. The only difference is the zip: pulled down with the jacket opening here, pulled up to the chin with the jacket closed there.
example_nl: Binnen rits ik mijn jas open.
alt: Een volwassene trekt het lipje van een jas omlaag en de twee helften wijken uit elkaar.

scene: SKIP: its partner leeglopen is dropped (Bijvoeglijke naamwoorden owns leeggelopen), and no separable verb that one visible change tells apart is left to pair with.
must: a stream from the tap and a half-full tub with an upward arrow.
avoid: water swirling down the open plug hole (leeglopen); a hand turning a tap (opendraaien); a glass being filled (not the card); a person in the bath (not the card).
contrast: Pair with leeglopen. The only difference is the water: pouring in from the tap here, swirling out down the plug hole there.
example_nl: Het bad loopt langzaam vol.
alt: Uit de kraan stroomt water in een half gevuld bad met de stop erin.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of Bijvoeglijke naamwoorden leeggelopen (owner ruling 20 November: the adjective keeps the word).
must: a spiral swirl at the open plug hole with a downward arrow.
avoid: water pouring in from the tap (vollopen); a tap being turned off (dichtdraaien); a bucket emptied into a sink (not the card); a flat bicycle tyre (not the card).
contrast: Pair with vollopen. The only difference is the water: swirling out down the plug hole here, pouring in from the tap there.
example_nl: Het bad loopt heel langzaam leeg.
alt: Het water in een bad draait in een kolk naar het open afvoergat en de stop ligt ernaast.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Three spectators on a low stand raise both arms high and shout with broad open smiles towards the player on the field, short burst lines round their hands; the player runs with the ball below them.
must: three spectators with arms raised high and broad open smiles.
avoid: spectators with thumbs down and frowning shouts (uitjouwen); a player sitting on a bench watching (toekijken); a team lifting a cup (winnen); a party with balloons (vieren); a person waving goodbye (not the card).
contrast: Pair with uitjouwen. The only difference is the spectators: arms up and smiling here, thumbs down and frowning there.
example_nl: Ik moedig mijn zus luid aan.
example_en: I cheer my sister on loudly.
alt: Drie toeschouwers steken lachend hun armen omhoog naar een speler op het veld.

scene: One drawing, one panel. Three spectators on the same low stand hold their thumbs down towards the player on the field and shout with wide frowning mouths, short jagged lines coming from them; the player runs with the ball below them.
must: three spectators with thumbs down and wide frowning mouths.
avoid: spectators with arms raised and smiling (aanmoedigen); a person shouting into a phone (not the card); a person looking away (wegkijken); a player stepping onto the pitch (invallen).
contrast: Pair with aanmoedigen. The only difference is the spectators: thumbs down and frowning here, arms up and smiling there.
example_nl: Het publiek jouwt de speler uit.
alt: Drie toeschouwers steken boos hun duimen omlaag naar een speler op het veld.

scene: SKIP: its partner oppompen is dropped (Bijvoeglijke naamwoorden owns opgepompt), and blowing up by mouth alone is the Werkwoorden blazen picture.
must: puffed cheeks with the lips round the mattress valve.
avoid: a foot pump with a hose on the valve (oppompen); a person blowing out a candle (uitblazen); a person holding the breath with puffed cheeks (inhouden); a person asleep on the mattress (not the card).
contrast: Pair with oppompen. The only difference is what fills the mattress: the mouth of the adult at the valve here, a foot pump with a hose there.
example_nl: Ik blaas het luchtbed helemaal op.
example_en: I blow up the air mattress completely.
alt: Een volwassene heeft de lippen om het ventiel van een half leeg luchtbed en bolle wangen.

scene: SKIP: duplicate of Bijvoeglijke naamwoorden opgepompt (owner ruling 20 November: the adjective keeps the word).
must: a foot pump pressed down with its hose on the mattress valve.
avoid: lips round the valve with puffed cheeks (opblazen); a bicycle tyre being pumped (not the card); a foot on a car pedal (not the card); a balloon being tied (not the card).
contrast: Pair with opblazen. The only difference is what fills the mattress: a foot pump with a hose here, the mouth of the adult at the valve there.
example_nl: Ik pomp het luchtbed snel op.
example_en: I pump up the air mattress quickly.
alt: Een volwassene trapt op een pedaal met een slang naar het ventiel van een half leeg luchtbed.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult tips a pan of cooked pasta over a colander in the sink, a stream of water and pasta pouring into it and steam rising, water running out of the holes of the colander below; a small arrow points down into the sink. The plate on the counter stays empty.
must: a tipped pan pouring pasta and water into a colander in the sink.
avoid: pasta spooned from the pan onto a plate (opscheppen); a person pouring coffee (not the card); a sieve shaken over a bowl (not the card); dishes washed in a sink (afwassen).
contrast: Pair with opscheppen. The only difference is where the pasta goes: into the colander in the sink here, onto the plate there.
example_nl: Ik giet de pasta voorzichtig af.
alt: Een volwassene kiept een pan met pasta en water boven een schaal met gaatjes in de spoelbak.

scene: One drawing, one panel. An adult holds the same pan of cooked pasta tilted over the plate on the counter and lifts a heap of pasta onto it with a large spoon, a little steam rising; a small arrow points down onto the plate. The colander in the sink stays empty.
must: a large spoon lifting pasta from the pan onto the plate.
avoid: pasta and water poured into a colander (afgieten); a person eating up a plate of food (opeten); a plate set down at a laid table (klaarzetten); a stew stirred on a stove (not the card).
contrast: Pair with afgieten. The only difference is where the pasta goes: onto the plate here, into the colander in the sink there.
example_nl: Ik schep voor iedereen pasta op.
example_en: I serve up pasta for everyone.
alt: Een volwassene legt met een grote lepel pasta uit een pan op een bord.
